strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap: existing methods (LESS, DSIR, TSDS) assume large in-domain pools and validation sets absent in truly low-resource settings
Novel empirical observation of stable NTK-like behavior in LLMs during LoRA fine-tuning (Frobenius cosine similarity >0.99), enabling efficient data selection without recomputation
Clever Jacobian-free NTK approximation that reduces computational burden while preserving relative magnitude information (~6% cross-terms empirically validated)
Comprehensive experimental validation: 8 tasks across 4 domains, 2 model architectures, consistent improvements (8.7/5.3 point gains, 10.9×/5.7× vs domain-only), and useful ablations
Strong empirical validation of NTK-like behavior via kernel ridge regression achieving 90% of fine-tuning accuracy (Table 3) and correlation analysis (Figure 2b)
Practical significance with substantial real-world improvements and honest discussion of computational costs and limitations
weaknesses: Insufficient statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests reported; test sets limited to 1K samples without variance analysis

Theory-practice gap: NTK-like behavior is empirically observed but not theoretically proven; no mechanistic explanation for why it emerges; perturbation bounds depend on unknown ε with unclear practical guidance

Suspicious baseline comparisons: LESS shows catastrophic failure on some tasks (49.8-point drop on FPB for Qwen3-8B), suggesting potential hyperparameter tuning issues that undermine validity of comparisons
Limited auxiliary data diversity: all experiments use single corpus (CoT Collection); generalization to diverse or out-of-distribution auxiliary sources unexplored

Unjustified design choices: greedy top-N selection ignores diversity (no comparison with diversity-aware methods); utility score design unablated; no sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters (random projection seed, K, warm-up epochs)
High computational cost (31 hours on A100 GPU) limits practical adoption despite claims of 'favorable scaling'; bottleneck analysis missing
Incomplete methodological details: embedding computation details sparse; sensitivity to warm-up LoRA training not analyzed; CoT responses generated via GPT-4o-mini introduces potential bias
Limited scope: only LoRA fine-tuning tested; generalization to full fine-tuning or other adaptation methods unknown; cold-start scenarios with <1K domain samples untested
Missing ablations: no direct comparison of two-stage vs single-stage NTK selection; simpler baselines (gradient-based weighting) absent; impact of embedding pre-selection not isolated

strengths: Addresses practical problem of data selection for low-resource domains with no validation sets
Consistent empirical improvements across 8 diverse tasks and 4 domains (only method improving all tasks)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning medical, financial, legal, and psychological domains
Clear algorithmic design with sensible two-stage approach combining embedding filtering and gradient-based scoring
Detailed documentation of hyperparameters, training setup, and algorithmic details
weaknesses: Weak theoretical foundation: NTK-like behavior (Definition 1) deviates from classical NTK assumptions; connection between kernel behavior and utility score (Eq. 11) is not rigorously justified; Theorem 1's perturbation bound is loose and practical implications unclear
Unfair baseline comparisons: LESS and TSDS designed for in-domain corpora with validation sets; running on out-of-domain corpus with minimal warm-up artificially inflates NTK-Selector advantage
Confounding factor from GPT-4o-mini: Training data lacks chain-of-thought, so GPT-4o-mini generates it; improvements may come from CoT generation rather than selection method; relegated to appendix

Experimental rigor issues: No significance testing or confidence intervals; small test sets (1K samples); high variance in results (Qwen3-8B shows 49.8-point LESS failure); results unstable across models

Missing critical ablations: No ablation on LoRA parameter restriction's effect on NTK-like behavior; no comparison of Jacobian-free vs. exact NTK; no analysis of random projection impact; sensitivity to M,K limited

Limited novelty: Two-stage filtering (embedding → gradient similarity) is standard; Jacobian-free approximation is straightforward; random projection is direct application of existing lemma; NTK-like behavior is primarily empirical observation

Scalability and practical limitations: 31 hours on A100 GPU; performance plateaus at ×10 auxiliary samples with diminishing returns; requires 1.8M-sample candidate corpus; 10:1 auxiliary-to-domain ratio may be unrealistic

Overstated theoretical contributions: Claims 'first work to empirically investigate kernel behavior' but previous work (Malladi et al., Wei et al.) has explored this; NTK-like behavior is modest observation, not fundamental insight
Missing simpler baselines: No comparison to basic embedding similarity selection or other gradient-based methods; unclear what machinery specifically from NTK contributes
Unstable results for Qwen3-8B: Extreme variance in results not adequately explained or investigated; high sensitivity to model architecture

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing a genuine gap in existing data selection methods that assume large validation sets and in-domain pools
Novel empirical insight that LLMs exhibit NTK-like behavior during fine-tuning, supported by Theorem 1 showing training dynamics can be approximated by initial kernel with bounded perturbation
Practical two-stage framework combining embedding-based pre-selection and Jacobian-free NTK selection, with computational cost reduced to ~31 hours for 1.8M samples
Strong and consistent empirical results: 10.9× and 5.7× improvements over domain-only baseline across both models, with improvements on every single task tested
Comprehensive experimental validation across 8 diverse tasks (medical, financial, legal, psychological), 2 models, multiple strong baselines, and thorough ablation studies (Figures 3-5, Tables 2-3)
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, training configuration, case studies of selected samples, and complete algorithm description
Outperforms multiple sophisticated baselines (LESS, DSIR, TSDS) that often fail or degrade performance, especially for stronger models like Qwen3-8B
weaknesses: Empirical evidence for NTK-like behavior generality is limited: Figure 2a shows only one task (financial sentiment) for two models; comprehensive analysis across all 8 tasks and other domains not provided

Loose theoretical justification: Theorem 1 establishes training dynamics ≈ initial kernel + perturbation, but the selection criterion (average NTK similarity) is not explicitly derived from this theory or the bi-level optimization problem
Incomplete validation of Jacobian-free approximation: While Figure 2b shows correlation, analysis of how ~6% cross-term error affects sample ranking (not just values) is missing
Two-stage design insufficiently justified: Embedding-based pre-selection uses a different proximity metric than NTK; ablation comparing pure NTK selection or sensitivity to M=4N choice is lacking
Table 3 (eNTK regression validation) excludes medical tasks due to label issues, providing incomplete evidence for the core NTK-like behavior hypothesis; 5-10% gap unexplored

Limited analysis of when auxiliary data helps vs. hurts: Llama3 improves with random selection while Qwen3-8B degrades; no systematic investigation of model/domain characteristics affecting performance
All 8 tasks are classification/Q&A with generated CoT format; generalization to generation tasks, other modalities, or different task structures is unknown
Method assumes access to large general-domain corpus (1.8M examples); applicability when such data unavailable not discussed despite claiming to address low-resource scenarios
Multiple hyperparameters (M, K, projection dimension, warm-up regime) with incomplete guidance on setting them without validation sets; sensitivity analysis not comprehensive
Computational cost remains substantial at 31 hours despite optimizations; practical applicability for resource-constrained settings questionable

strengths: First systematic investigation of NTK-like behavior in LLMs during fine-tuning, demonstrating remarkable stability (>0.99 Frobenius similarity) across diverse models, tasks, and hyperparameter settings
Comprehensive experimental validation across 8 tasks in 4 domains with multiple strong baselines (DSIR, LESS, TSDS), two model architectures, and extensive ablation studies demonstrating consistency

Practical two-stage framework (embedding pre-selection + NTK scoring) with efficient approximations (LoRA, random projection) makes method scalable; 31-hour selection cost is justified by 10.9x/5.7x improvement over domain-only baseline

Well-motivated approach: Jacobian-free NTK approximation is theoretically justified (Theorem 3.2 with bounded perturbation analysis) and empirically validated (cross-output gradient orthogonality ~0.02)
Addresses important real-world problem of low-resource domain adaptation where direct fine-tuning on 1K domain samples causes severe overfitting (e.g., 18.8-point drop on ContractNLI)
Robust across settings: NTK-Selector is the only method that improves all 8 tasks, whereas LESS/TSDS/DSIR fail dramatically on some (e.g., LESS drops 49.8 points on FPB with QWEN3-8B)
Strong reproducibility: extensive implementation details, prompt templates, hyperparameter choices, and theoretical proofs in comprehensive appendices
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: NTK-like behavior is empirically observed but not theoretically guaranteed for finite-width pretrained LLMs; Assumptions E.1-E.2 (isotropic LM head, Jacobian isotropy) are plausible but unverified for specific checkpoints
CoT-generation dependency: Synthetic reasoning from GPT-4o-mini introduces external model bias; performance depends on generative model quality; missing ablation on CoT quality impact

Computational overhead significant (31 hours on A100) but inadequately discussed in practical contexts; while compute-matched comparison (Table 12) is provided, selection cost should be more prominent in recommendations

Empirical improvements often modest: +1-3 points on many tasks (e.g., MMLU-Med +1.5, TFNS +3.8); largest gains occur when domain-only severely degrades (atypical); Qwen3-8B improvements smaller (+5.3 avg)

Limited technical novelty: applies established NTK theory (Jacot et al. 2018) to LLMs; Jacobian-free approximation (summing outputs) is straightforward; two-stage selection is standard in data selection literature

Evaluation gaps: (1) no validation-set-aware comparison (unrealistic assumption); (2) no statistical significance testing/confidence intervals; (3) inconsistent metrics across tasks; (4) missing analysis of failure modes (e.g., LESS drops)

Experimental design dependencies: warm-up LoRA training required for pre-selection; CoT generation limited to specific tasks; generalization to generation tasks, multimodal domains, or other auxiliary corpora unexplored

Presentation density: key details (related work, prompt templates) in appendices; Figure 1 radar chart hard to read; Table 1 has too many columns; NTK-link-to-selection-quality explanation could be clearer

strengths: Addresses a practical problem with clear motivation: leveraging general-domain data for low-resource domain adaptation
Empirically demonstrates NTK-like behavior (>0.99 Frobenius similarity) in LLMs with extensive validation across architectures and fine-tuning strategies
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 tasks in 4 domains with thorough ablation studies and design analysis
Practical algorithmic design using LoRA and random projection makes the approach reasonably scalable
Consistent improvements demonstrated across multiple domains and model sizes
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: Jacobian-free NTK approximation is a straightforward simplification; using kernel similarity for data selection is well-established; two-stage approach is standard in prior work

Weak theoretical justification: Theorem 3.2 bounds dynamics deviation but does not justify why NTK ranking should select good samples; eNTK regression achieves only 90% of fine-tuning accuracy (Table 3), showing significant approximation error; high-dimensional assumptions (E.1-E.2) are informally justified without direct validation

Problematic empirical validation: Domain-only baseline performs worse than random selection on multiple tasks, suggesting hyperparameter mismatch; LESS induces 49.8-point drop on FPB; random selection is highly competitive at larger scales (Figure 3); synthetic CoT data raises quality concerns; no statistical significance tests
High computational cost: ~31 hours on A100 for selecting 9K samples; no cost-benefit analysis; warm-up stage adds overhead but Table 13 shows its removal causes minimal degradation

Limited scope and generalization: Only instruction-tuned models, LoRA fine-tuning, 8B-scale models; no evaluation on base models, full fine-tuning, or larger models; arbitrary hyperparameter choices (N=9K, M=4N) lack principled justification
Fundamental motivation gap: No clear explanation for why NTK alignment (feature-space metric) should correlate with semantic relevance for cross-domain adaptation
Dense presentation with overly long appendices; core contributions obscured by implementation details; missing comparisons with recent gradient-based selection and influence function variants

strengths: Well-motivated and practical problem formulation: addresses realistic low-resource domain adaptation without requiring task-specific validation sets, filling a gap between existing methods and real-world constraints

Convincing empirical validation of NTK-like behavior: Frobenius cosine similarity >0.99 across 4 model architectures, 3 fine-tuning strategies, and extended training (50 epochs), extending prior work beyond small models

Principled yet scalable method: Theorem 3.2 provides theoretical foundation, Jacobian-free approximation (Eq. 5) achieves >0.95 Spearman correlation with standard NTK while reducing computation, LoRA integration enables practical application

Comprehensive experimental validation: consistent improvements on all 8 tasks (vs. baselines showing inconsistency), extensive ablations (Figures 3-5, Tables 2, 12-15), compute-matched baseline (Table 12) confirms gains from data quality not just quantity

Robust and generalizable results: NTK-Selector works uniformly across diverse domains (medical, financial, legal, psychological) while LESS/DSIR/TSDS show large negative results on individual tasks (e.g., -49.8 points)
Detailed reproducibility: hyperparameters, runtime analysis (Table 4), overlap verification (Table 14), case studies (Figures 14-16) demonstrating method captures meaningful reasoning patterns
Honest insights about fine-tuning: acknowledges domain-only overfitting phenomenon, provides grounded hypothesis about model capacity differences between Llama3 and Qwen3
weaknesses: Theoretical gap in core justification: NTK-like behavior describes optimization dynamics but paper doesn't rigorously establish why high NTK similarity to domain samples improves downstream task performance; connection between kernel values and generalization absent

Strong unvalidated assumptions in Jacobian-free approximation: Assumptions E.1 (isotropic LM head) and E.2 (Jacobian Gram structure) rely on Neural Collapse phenomena from classification tasks; limited empirical verification these hold for language modeling; high-dimensional error bound O(d^{-1/2} + √r/d) asymptotic with unclear practical validity

Experimental rigor concerns: (1) CoT responses generated by GPT-4o-mini for tasks lacking annotations, introducing potential bias and quality variability; (2) some tasks use 1K random test subset rather than full test set; (3) LESS baseline uses only 0.1% pre-selection while NTK-Selector uses full pool, potentially unfair comparison; (4) only 3 runs, no confidence intervals, improvements sometimes modest (1-2 points) without significance testing

Substantial computational cost without baseline comparison: 31-hour runtime on A100 GPU for selection, no comparison with LESS/DSIR/TSDS costs; unclear practical viability for resource-constrained settings

Design choices lack principled justification: (1) simple averaging utility score (s_j = average NTK) without exploring weighted/learned aggregation; (2) embedding-based pre-selection assumes semantic similarity equals utility, unexplored failure modes; (3) hyperparameters (M, K, p) empirically tuned with no selection rules provided

Limited scope and missing analyses: (1) all experiments use LoRA + instruction tuning despite claiming generality; (2) only Cot Collection tested as candidate pool; (3) very low-resource regime (|D|≤50) unexplored despite being most critical; (4) no failure case analysis or task characteristic prediction; (5) generation tasks absent

Synthetic data and CoT sensitivity: claims all methods use same domain-CoT supervision, but synthetic generation by GPT-4o-mini may bias results; only example-based ablation (Appendix H.9) rather than systematic sensitivity study
